subject.title: feat(slack): Support Slack RTS (Real-Time Search) API via assistant action tokens

question: Should OpenClaw add Slack RTS as a separate assistant action-token search path, and what token containment, read-target policy, and scope rules should it use?
rationale: The missing source path is clear, but Slack RTS authorizes workspace search with event-scoped credentials, so automation should not choose the permanent product/security boundary.

options.title: Approve narrow RTS contract
options.body: Implement `assistant.search.context` inside the Slack plugin with event-scoped token containment, approved read-target/privacy enforcement, docs, tests, and redacted live Slack proof.

options.title: Consolidate Slack search first
options.body: Define one Slack search contract covering RTS and any user-token search path before accepting implementation work.

options.title: Defer workspace search
options.body: Keep the issue open but block implementation until maintainers are ready to own Slack workspace-search privacy and token semantics.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow RTS contract
recommendation.body: Implement `assistant.search.context` inside the Slack plugin with event-scoped token containment, approved read-target/privacy enforcement, docs, tests, and redacted live Slack proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest recent Slack assistant/action history and already routed broad Slack search work back to this issue.
